react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by a single, powerfully coherent story: arachidonic acid metabolism and eicosanoid biosynthesis. Across three orthogonal paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 1.39×10⁻¹²), Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p = 0.006), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (rank 1) — the same pathway cluster emerges as the unambiguous winner. The five eicosanoid-driver metabolites (arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2, and leukotriene A4) form a tight metabolic module that branches from arachidonic acid via three distinct enzymatic axes: the 5-lipoxygenase arm producing leukotriene A4 and 5-HETE, the 15-lipoxygenase arm producing 15-HETE, and the cyclooxygenase/arm generating the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15-deoxy-PGJ2. The massive fold-enrichment of 1250.95 (RaMP) reflects the fact that 5 of 27 pathway members are present in a 9-metabolite input set — a 1250-fold overrepresentation. L-serine contributes a secondary signal through glycerophospholipid metabolism (Mummichog rank 2, p = 0.019), consistent with its role in phosphatidylserine biosynthesis. Dehydroascorbic acid, methylmalonic acid, and 6-methylmercaptopurine do not achieve significance in any paradigm and likely represent non-pathway background or treatment-specific off-target effects. The biological interpretation is of a selective perturbation of the arachidonic acid cascade, implicating cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase pathways in the experimental treatment with high confidence.

The KEGG-namespace baseline from MetaboAnalystR PSEA (run_metaboanalystr_psea) independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) with four overlapping hits, while m/z-direct analysis via Mummichog (run_mummichog) scored Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top network hit (p = 0.0072) and also identified Glycerophospholipid metabolism (p = 0.018) and Leukotriene metabolism (p = 0.052). Arachidonic acid is the canonical substrate for three enzymatic fates — the 5-lipoxygenase branch (5-HETE → leukotriene A4), the 12/15-lipoxygenase branch (15-HETE) — and the cyclooxygenase branch (15-deoxy-PGJ2). The convergence of four compounds across all three paradigms, anchored by arachidonic acid itself, strongly implicates phospholipase A2-mediated membrane release followed by eicosanoid biosynthesis as the primary perturbed pathway. L-Serine (C00065) additionally connected to glycerophospholipid metabolism via the mummichog network, suggesting a secondary perturbation of membrane lipid remodelling. The three remaining metabolites — dehydroascorbic acid, methylmalonic acid, and 6-methylmercaptopurine — were not enriched in any top pathway, indicating they are unlikely to be primary drivers in this experimental context.
